title: Spain's Manza Energía tops first EU energy communities prize
dek: Ten citizen-led energy communities from six countries share €1 million in the first EU Prize for Governance Innovations in Energy Communities.
key_facts: Prize for Governance Innovations in Energy Communities (first edition)
€1 million, shared by 10 communities from 6 countries
Manza Energía (ES) €350,000 · Robin Powerhood (AT) €200,000 · Viver Telheiras (PT) €100,000
€50,000 each, incl. CERCA and Manresa Il·lumina (ES)
Horizon Europe Cluster 5 (Climate, Energy and Mobility); managed by CINEA
body: The European Commission awarded its first Prize for Governance Innovations in Energy Communities on 10 November 2026, during the European Research and Innovation Days in Brussels. Ten citizen-led communities from six countries share €1 million, after each finalist pitched its governance model to the audience.

Manza Energía from Spain took the largest prize, €350,000, followed by Robin Powerhood from Austria with €200,000 and Viver Telheiras from Portugal with €100,000. Seven more communities receive €50,000 each: Ketelhuis WG (Netherlands), CERCA (Spain), brupower (Belgium), Manresa Il·lumina (Spain), ECoOB (Belgium), and Minoa Energeiaki and Hyperion (Greece). Spain is the country with the most winners, three of the ten.

The prize was open to renewable and citizen energy communities as defined in EU law with up to 10,000 members. An independent jury scored how inclusive the governance structure is, the internal governance process, the links to the local and regional transition, and other innovative approaches. According to the Commission, the winners show communities that are open to everyone, give each member one vote in general assemblies and open leadership roles to women and young members.

The prize is funded under Cluster 5 (Climate, Energy and Mobility) of Horizon Europe and managed by CINEA. The Commission plans to keep working with the ten winners so that other energy communities across Europe can learn from them, for example through lessons-learnt workshops.
why: Ullswater Investments analysis: inducement prizes reward results already achieved rather than a project plan, so they suit organisations that have built something that works but would struggle with a full Horizon Europe proposal. Spain's strong showing confirms that Spanish energy communities can compete at EU level. Communities, cooperatives and municipalities with an inclusive governance model should keep an eye on future Horizon Europe prizes, and use this recognition as evidence of track record when applying to other EU or national calls on the energy transition.
